newsitem.title: JORDAN: Accused killer of Israelis faces sentence Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Accused killer of Israelis faces sentence Saturday.

text.p: A Jordanian military court trying a soldier for premeditated murder of seven Israeli schoolgirls said on Sunday it would announce its verdict on Saturday.

Brigadier Mamoun al-Khasawneh set the date after an expert witness said under Jordanian law army private Ahmed Daqamsa had "diminished responsibility" for his actions because he suffered from personality problems.
Daqamsa has not denied shooting the schoolgirls on their visit to the Jordanian border territory of Baqoura four months ago and could face the death sentence if found guilty.

But Doctor Awni Saad, a psychologist summoned by the court to shed light on Daqamsa's state of mind, said the soldier's "anti-social personality disorder" meant he acted with disregard for the consequences.
Saad said this ruled out the charge of premeditation in murder cases.
Military prosecutors and Daqamsa's defence lawyers have both summoned psychiatric specialists in the final stages of the trial to validate their cases.
Prosecutors portray Daqamsa as a scheming, deviant assassin, while his defence team say he is a pious and patriotic man with mental problems, who opened fire after provocation.

Professor Nizam Abu Hijleh, summoned along with Doctor Saad by the five-man panel of military judges to cut through the conflicting medical diagnoses, agreed that Daqamsa's disorder meant he had reduced responsibility.
Abu Hijleh said a typical sufferer "can plan (his actions), but in practice he rarely resorts to planning".
Daqamsa, wearing an olive-green jumpsuit, sat quietly behind the black bars of his cage in the dock, occasionally reading from the Koran.

Witnesses say Daqamsa opened fire on the seven schoolgirls aged between 11 and 13 while they were visiting Baqoura, a small patch of border land returned to Jordan by Israel under a 1994 peace treaty but then leased back to Israel.
The shooting revealed the deep rift in Jordanian opinion over the peace accord.

Jordan's vocal opponents of peace with Israel rallied around Daqamsa even though King Hussein, who has championed the peace treaty with Israel, denounced the shooting as a shameful act and flew to Jerusalem to pay condolence to families of the victims.
"As far as I was concerned those children were like my children. They were there enjoying a new atmosphere of peace," he said last week.
Daqamsa say the girls teased him while he was praying. Prosecution witnesses have denied he was praying, saying he had planned the attack carefully and hinted at his intentions to his army comrades.
